bk_50.subject: Extreme close-up, low angle: a lean hard-faced Filipino man in his thirties, brown skin, short black hair, a thin moustache, sunken cheeks, a loose white camisa shirt, a red kerchief around his neck, dark rolled trousers, shouting a question with his mouth open, stern eyes, his face lit by orange torchlight; a long steel blade catches the light at the bottom edge of the picture. His face in the upper half of the picture.
bk_50.setting: a wide trampled dirt yard among nipa huts on stilts, a big old wooden barn and bamboo groves in the countryside north of Manila, on a night in August 1896, hundreds of flaming torches; no modern buildings, no electric wires, no guns

bk_89.subject: Low-angle medium close-up hero portrait, chest up: a handsome young Filipino man about twenty, lean, warm brown skin, short tousled black hair tied in a small topknot, dark brown eyes, a red cloth headband with long tails, wearing a loose white collarless camisa shirt, a round bronze medallion on a cord around his neck. He looks straight at the viewer with a confident half-smile, one eyebrow slightly raised, chin a little lifted, like the charming lead of a film; the tails of the red headband and loose strands of his hair blow in the wind; strong jawline, bright eyes, the collar of the camisa open at the throat. His face is in the upper half of the picture, centred. Only one person in the picture; his arms are down, hands out of frame.
bk_89.setting: behind him a great turning ring of golden light and sparks like a gate in time, night sky above, a few torches and nipa huts of an 1896 camp far below and out of focus
bk_89.light: warm golden rim light from the ring behind him on his hair and shoulders, soft warm fill on his face, embers drifting, heroic and bright, shallow depth of field
bk_89.note: owner, 16 Nov: the line 'Ako 'to si Indio' must show Indio himself, as a heart-throb, not the dog

bk_05.subject: Over-the-shoulder shot from just behind his right shoulder: a young Filipino man about twenty, lean, warm brown skin, short tousled black hair tied in a small topknot, dark brown eyes, wearing a plain white short-sleeved polo shirt, black slacks, a small dark backpack on his shoulders, a round bronze medallion on a cord around his neck, a red handkerchief tied on his left wrist, no headband, no tattoos, leaning toward a thick glass service window, sliding a brown folder through the small slot with one hand; behind the glass, out of focus, a middle-aged Filipina clerk looking down at her desk. He is alone, no dog, no animals. The window and his face in the upper half.
bk_05.setting: a government office service window in Quezon City in our time: a thick glass pane with a small half-moon slot at counter level, a worn wooden counter, pale green walls, fluorescent tubes; no posters, no signs, no writing anywhere
bk_05.light: cold fluorescent light, a shaft of warm morning sun from the side, reflections on the glass, richly painted, detailed ink linework, textured brushwork

bk_15.subject: Wide shot at night in the rain: a young Filipino man about twenty, lean, warm brown skin, short tousled black hair tied in a small topknot, dark brown eyes, wearing a plain white short-sleeved polo shirt, black slacks, a small dark backpack on his shoulders, a round bronze medallion on a cord around his neck, a red handkerchief tied on his left wrist, no headband, no tattoos, soaking wet from the rain, falling backward onto the wet pavement, propped on his elbows, mouth open in shock; a body-length apart in front of him, standing inside a blinding burst of golden light, a medium-sized slim black short-haired Philippine street dog with a white chest patch, one folded ear and bright clever eyes, a red kerchief around his neck. The dog's left ear stands upright and pointed, only the dog's right ear is folded down; the dog's face is all black with no white on it, the white patch is only on the dog's chest. Four legs, one tail. Both in the upper half of the picture.
bk_15.setting: the Pugad Lawin Shrine in Bahay Toro, Quezon City, at night in heavy rain: a small concrete shelter roof by a low wall and an iron fence, big old acacia trees, an iron street lamp; no cross, no church, no religious statue
bk_15.light: a blinding golden flash from the light, raindrops lit gold, deep blue night, rim light, richly painted, detailed ink linework, textured brushwork

bk_80.subject: High crane shot looking straight down at night on a wide dirt yard: a big ring of small figures, a mixed crowd of Filipino country people of 1896, men, women and grey-haired elders, every one different: straw hats or bare heads, shirts of white, brown, dark blue and ochre, women in long dark skirts with hair in buns, some crouching, some pointing, some holding torches, none wears a headband. In the open middle of the ring, alone, a young Filipino man about twenty, lean, warm brown skin, short tousled black hair tied in a small topknot, dark brown eyes, a red cloth headband with long tails, wearing a loose white collarless camisa shirt, rolled-up red trousers, barefoot, a round bronze medallion on a cord around his neck, landing on his knees in the dust, small in the frame, the only person with a red headband, faces turning toward him. The nearest people at the bottom edge are dark silhouettes seen from behind.
bk_80.setting: a wide trampled dirt yard among nipa huts on stilts, a big old wooden barn and bamboo groves in the countryside north of Manila, on a night in August 1896, hundreds of flaming torches; no modern buildings, no electric wires, no guns
bk_80.light: night, hard orange firelight from many torches, deep black shadows, glowing embers in the air, rim light, smoke, richly painted, detailed ink linework, textured brushwork
bk_80.note: crowd of varied country people; only Indio has the headband

bk_86.subject: High wide shot from behind and above, the figure small in the lower half of the picture: a young Filipino man about twenty, lean, warm brown skin, short tousled black hair tied in a small topknot, dark brown eyes, wearing a plain white short-sleeved polo shirt, black slacks, a small dark backpack on his shoulders, a red handkerchief tied on his left wrist, no headband, no tattoos, soaking wet from the rain, standing alone at an iron railing above a street, seen from behind in three-quarter view from his left, the top of his head no higher than the middle of the picture; no necklace; his bare left forearm rests on the railing, the red handkerchief on the left wrist, three short slanted indigo strokes tattooed on the left forearm near the elbow; beyond the railing the wet street with two painted jeepneys.
